scenario: Alternating (paired) Wan stop, edit and resume on the GPU through the app API: Save and stop partway through a low-noise phase, a new Job revision with another preview prompt, a higher total and a doubled learning rate, then resume (#206)

hardware.gpu_power_note: The owner's fixed power limit (280 W of 350 W) and fan profile were left unchanged.

method.workspace: The same isolated GPU acceptance workspace, backend and request sequence as h3-resume.json. Configured native FP16 Wan 2.2 experts, Wan 2.1 VAE and UMT5 from the owner's settings, read only.
method.dataset: The workspace's synthetic Wan acceptance dataset: one generated 17-frame 256x256 16 fps clip with a one-line caption; one step per epoch.
method.stop: A poller sent POST /api/runs/{id}/control {save_and_stop} once the low-noise expert had trained 13 updates, partway through its third phase (low 10 to 15).
method.segment_controls: Save now when low reached 17, mid-phase. Sample now was refused with 409 'Sample now is unavailable: alternating Wan previews run as separate sampling stages.', as documented in runs-lifecycle.md; the segment's scheduled paired previews at 20, 30 and 40 and the final sample cover sampling.
method.vram_sampling: nvidia-smi whole-device memory.used every 2 s, grouped by each stage's recorded start and finish; includes about 870 MiB of desktop use.
method.step_time: Each phase's trainer timing record (training seconds excluding previews, divided by step intervals).

limits: Synthetic one-clip data at 256x256x17 and rank 8 proves the mechanics of resuming, not useful learning or production-size capacity.
Upstream restarts its data order at every phase, restored or not; with one clip per epoch this trial cannot show data-position effects.
Whole-device VRAM sampled every 2 s includes desktop use and can miss brief peaks.
